resources.string:
Forwarding mouse and keyboard to Android apps needs a small service with shell permissions. No root, and no other app to install. You only pair once.

1. Connect to Wi-Fi. It must be connected while you activate; the phone's own hotspot may not count. Losing Wi-Fi afterwards is fine.

2. Tap the button below to open Developer options, turn on “Wireless debugging”, then tap “Pair device with pairing code”. If there are no Developer options, tap the build number several times in “About phone” first.

3. The pairing dialog shows a 6-digit code. You can type it straight into XDesk's notification.

4. If the notification won't take it (seen on HyperOS), enter it below. Keep the pairing dialog open. If it closes when you switch back here, open Settings and XDesk together in split screen or a floating window.
Port after the colon in the pairing dialog

When you open XDesk with wireless debugging on, it starts the service by itself.

After the phone restarts, activate again: if the system allows it, XDesk turns on wireless debugging by itself while on Wi-Fi, otherwise it tells you what to do.

Don't turn off USB debugging or Developer options while it runs.
The pairing port is not known yet. Enter the number after the colon in the pairing dialog.
No pairing port found yet. If the pairing dialog is open, you can enter it yourself.
The system no longer has the pairing. Pair again.
Go back to XDesk and tap “Open wireless debugging settings” again.
Go back to XDesk to continue.
%1$s\nIf you can\'t type in the notification, go back to XDesk and enter the code there.
XDesk is looking for the pairing port

Turn on “Wireless debugging” and tap “Pair device with pairing code”. Keep the pairing dialog open. Once found, you can enter the code in this notification. If you can\'t, open XDesk in split screen or a floating window and enter it there.
Pairing port found, enter the code
Tap “Enter pairing code” and type the 6 digits from the pairing dialog. If you can\'t, open XDesk in split screen or a floating window and enter it there.
Can\'t find the wireless debugging port. Check in Developer options that wireless debugging is on, then come back.
The input service started but does not answer. Try again.
Wireless debugging refused XDesk. If you revoked the authorisation in Developer options, tap “Pair again” in XDesk\'s settings.
Can\'t reach the pairing port. The pairing dialog may have closed; open it again and retry.
Pairing failed. Check the code, and keep the pairing dialog open. (%1$s)
Wireless debugging is off. Turn it on in Developer options (Wi-Fi must be connected). XDesk continues when you come back.
XDesk can turn on wireless debugging by itself, but Wi-Fi must be connected first. The phone\'s own hotspot may not count. Come back once connected.
The system did not turn on wireless debugging. It needs Wi-Fi. If a dialog asks whether to allow this network, allow it and come back.
The system refused the injected input. On Xiaomi and Redmi phones, turn on “USB debugging (Security settings)” in Developer options.
Can\'t read the physical mouse and keyboard. The phone\'s touchpad still works: %1$s
XDesk is not connected to the input service
Some text can\'t be sent to Android apps as key presses (Chinese, for example)
Not supported on this Android version (%1$s)
This Android version has no way to clear the audio route
Can\'t change the phone\'s own screen
Can\'t list the tasks on the display: %1$s

The input service does not answer. Try again.
The input service did not start. Check in Shizuku that it is still running, then try again.
XDesk is running %1$s on the display
Can\'t create a display for the car: %1$s
Another app is already showing content on the display. It may cover %1$s

Forwarding mouse and keyboard to Android apps needs Shizuku (no root).
The Termux desktop doesn't need it.

Install and start Shizuku, then come back.
Open Shizuku and start it with wireless debugging as it explains,\nthen come back. XDesk continues by itself.

XDesk uses Shizuku to forward mouse and keyboard to the app on the display.

Run in Termux:

xdesk start

or any program: xdesk run command

A Termux desktop needs Termux. Install it from F-Droid or Termux's GitHub page,
then come back and choose again.

Android apps on the display don't need Termux.

Any device\'s browser as the display, over Wi-Fi or a USB cable
Serves a page on port 47150. The first time, a browser enters a 4-digit code shown on the phone.
Open an address below in a browser to see and use the display: picture, sound, mouse and keyboard. One browser or receiver at a time. Keep XDesk open on the phone.
Connect to Wi-Fi, turn on the hotspot, or USB tethering with a cable.

Connect an iPad, Mac or computer with a USB cable and turn on USB tethering (below). A wired address appears above. Lower and steadier delay than Wi-Fi. For iPad and Mac, switch tethering to NCM first. The phone barely charges from an iPad meanwhile.
iPad and Mac only work with NCM; Windows and Linux work with either. Turn USB tethering off and on after changing it.
